nodes.label: ProShottr Cross-Platform Build Plan
nodes.rationale: The 'how' document implementing every feature in feature.md across Android, Linux (X11+Wayland), Windows, macOS; combines WeChat speed-to-share with Shottr pro-precision.

nodes.label: Rust core + Flutter UI (Option A)
nodes.rationale: Chosen stack: one Flutter UI codebase across Android+3 desktops, a fast portable Rust core for capture/stitch/CV/image/OCR/upload, and Skia out-of-the-box for the annotation canvas. Proven by RustDesk. A recommendation not a mandate: pure-Flutter (Option E) is an acceptable MVP fallback; fully-native (Option C) wins on polish at highest cost.

nodes.label: One core, many shells (principle)
nodes.rationale: Perf-critical logic lives once in the shared native core; each platform contributes only capture/overlay/permission adapters + UI glue. Abstraction at the OS seam: every OS-specific capability sits behind a trait with a per-platform implementation.

nodes.label: Non-destructive vector editing (principle)
nodes.rationale: The editor manipulates a vector scene graph; rasterization happens only on export/copy so annotations stay re-editable until output.

nodes.label: Local-first, cloud-optional (principle)
nodes.rationale: Everything works offline; no account required for core use; cloud/S3 upload and sync are opt-in. No network unless the user uploads/syncs; telemetry off by default.

nodes.label: Two-speed UX (Quick + Pro)
nodes.rationale: A WeChat-like frictionless default path for casual sharing plus a Shottr-depth Pro editor one keypress away; default flow must be sub-second, Pro tools reachable without rasterizing annotations.

nodes.label: ScreenCapturer trait
nodes.rationale: Capture contract: list_displays/windows, capture_region/window/display, begin_stream (scrolling+recording), and supports() capability probe so the UI can gray out or reroute features a platform can't provide.

nodes.label: OverlayHost trait
nodes.rationale: Region-selection UI + pins: show_selection_overlay, create_pin_window, set_topmost; also the surface for the OCR result window and live coordinate/color HUD.

nodes.label: HotkeyManager trait
nodes.rationale: Registration/dispatch abstraction across OSes plus platform_trigger_surface substitutes (Android tile/bubble, Wayland GlobalShortcuts portal) where real global hotkeys don't exist.

nodes.label: TextRecognizer trait
nodes.rationale: OCR contract: recognize(image, langs) and decode_qr; best-per-platform backend (Vision/Windows.Media.Ocr/ML Kit) with PaddleOCR/Tesseract fallback for Chinese and offline uniformity.

nodes.label: ClipboardService trait
nodes.rationale: put_image/put_text/get_color_at abstraction over per-OS clipboard/selection mechanisms.

nodes.label: PermissionBroker trait
nodes.rationale: ensure(Capability) -> PermissionState for screen-record/overlay/accessibility/files; progressive permissions asked only when a feature is first used, degrading gracefully when denied.

nodes.label: Capture orchestrator (Rust)
nodes.rationale: Core 'capture' module driving the ScreenCapturer backends; capture pipeline freezes a full frame then shows the selection overlay over it for instant, flicker-free region select.

nodes.label: Annotation scene graph (non-destructive)
nodes.rationale: Ordered typed vector objects (Rect/Ellipse/Arrow/Path/Text/BlurRegion/Spotlight/StepBadge/ImageOverlay) with transform/style/z-index; undo/redo is a command stack; Flutter CustomPainter paints live while the Rust render module produces identical headless raster on export.

nodes.label: Scrolling-capture stitcher (CV)
nodes.rationale: Highest-risk feature: open a capture stream, detect vertical overlap between frames via normalized cross-correlation/feature matching, ignore sticky headers/footers, stitch into one tall image; Android uses AccessibilityService scroll, Wayland is degraded, with a manual-frame fallback.

nodes.label: OCR orchestrator (Rust)
nodes.rationale: Routes to the best TextRecognizer backend per platform/language; post-processes line-break stripping and layout ordering, QR via zxing/rqrr; translate is a separate pluggable provider off by default for privacy.

nodes.label: Rasterizer / render module (Rust)
nodes.rationale: Composites base image + scene to PNG/JPEG/auto and encodes before/after GIF; guarantees export output is identical headless for CLI/automation.

nodes.label: flutter_rust_bridge (Dart<->Rust FFI)
nodes.rationale: Codegen FFI seam connecting the Flutter UI to the shared Rust core; contract-tested per call.

nodes.label: .proshot document format
nodes.rationale: Re-openable non-destructive document = base image + scene serialized as JSON/CBOR; history/index kept in SQLite (rusqlite).

nodes.label: Quick HUD (WeChat-parity toolbar)
nodes.rationale: Tiny floating post-capture toolbar matching the verified WeChat spec (filled rect, outline ellipse, sticker picker, arrow, brush, mosaic manual+AI-mask, text 3 sizes, undo) with a prominent Send/Copy/Save/Pin; must degrade gracefully on narrow selections instead of silently repositioning.

nodes.label: Pro editor / annotation canvas
nodes.rationale: Full Shottr-depth canvas: left tool rail, right inspector (style/opacity/stroke), top capture-mode bar, bottom status (dimensions/zoom/color); reachable one keypress from the Quick HUD.

nodes.label: Windows adapter (WGC/DXGI/GDI)
nodes.rationale: Windows.Graphics.Capture primary GPU path (needs 1803+), DXGI Desktop Duplication for fullscreen/recording, PrintWindow/GDI fallback for stubborn windows; RegisterHotKey + WS_EX_LAYERED|TOPMOST overlays.

nodes.label: macOS adapter (ScreenCaptureKit)
nodes.rationale: ScreenCaptureKit (12.3+) primary with CGWindowListCreateImage fallback; requires Screen Recording TCC permission, hardened runtime + notarization; borderless floating NSPanel overlays.

nodes.label: Linux X11 adapter (XShm)
nodes.rationale: XShmGetImage (MIT-SHM) with XGetImage fallback, XRandR multi-monitor geometry, XGrabKey hotkeys, override-redirect fullscreen overlay + _NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE pins.

nodes.label: Linux Wayland adapter (portals/PipeWire)
nodes.rationale: The single hardest surface: Wayland's security model forbids arbitrary screen reads, so capture goes through consent-brokered portals (ScreenCast/PipeWire or Screenshot) or wlr-screencopy on wlroots; behavior differs across mutter/kwin/wlroots so a capability probe + per-compositor test matrix is required, and it's tackled early because it constrains architecture.

nodes.label: Android adapter (MediaProjection)
nodes.rationale: A different paradigm: sandboxed MediaProjection via a foreground service, consent dialog per session, no global hotkeys (bubble/QS-tile/notification/share-sheet triggers), SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW overlays, scrolling via AccessibilityService (opt-in), ML Kit OCR.

nodes.label: RustDesk reference architecture
nodes.rationale: Cited proof that Rust-core + Flutter-UI works for this exact problem shape across Windows/macOS/Linux/Android, using MediaProjection on Android and PipeWire/portals on Wayland.

nodes.label: Phased development roadmap
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 foundations -> Phase 1 desktop MVP (WeChat parity, Win+macOS) -> Phase 2 Linux X11+Wayland parity -> Phase 3 Pro tools -> Phase 4 sharing/cloud -> Phase 5 Android -> Phase 6 polish/1.0. Sequencing rationale: desktop-first delivers a usable tool fastest and de-risks capture/overlay abstractions before Android's different paradigm; Wayland tackled early because it constrains architecture and shouldn't be discovered late.
